# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 52 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 52 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_052_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 3 — Trees in Winter: You Cannot Tell the Righteous from the Sinners

**52:1** He showed me many trees that had no leaves, but which seemed to me to be withered; for they all appeared alike. And he said to me: "Do you see these trees?" "I see them, lord," I said; "they all appear alike and are withered." He answered and said to me: "These trees that you see are those who live in this present age."

**52:2** "Why then, lord," I said, "do they seem withered and alike?" "Because," he said, "neither the righteous nor the sinners are visible in this present age, but they resemble one another. For this age is winter for the righteous who live in it, and they are not visible among the sinners.

**52:3** For as in winter the trees, having shed their leaves, are all alike and it is not apparent which are dry and which are living — so also in this present age, the righteous are not visible, nor the sinners, but they all appear alike to one another."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the eschatological economy of Similitude 3.*
